`FastAPI.openapi()` (in `fastapi/applications.py`) calls `fastapi.openapi.utils.get_openapi()` to actually build the OpenAPI schema dict, passing in the app's title/version/routes/webhooks/tags/etc.

What makes repeated calls cheap is caching:

- `FastAPI.openapi()` first computes `routes_version = self.router._get_routes_version()` and only rebuilds/calls `get_openapi(...)` if `self.openapi_schema` is not yet set or if `self._openapi_routes_version != routes_version`. Otherwise it just returns the cached `self.openapi_schema` (`fastapi/applications.py`, lines ~1070–1102).
- `self.openapi_schema` is the cached schema dict (initialized to `None` and set after the first build).
- `self._openapi_routes_version` (`fastapi/applications.py:925`) stores the router version at the time the cache was last built, so subsequent calls can cheaply detect whether routes changed.
- `_get_routes_version()`/`_mark_routes_changed()` on `APIRouter` (`fastapi/routing.py`, around lines 2566–2584) maintain an integer `_routes_version` counter that's bumped whenever routes are mutated, and `_get_routes_version()` recursively sums the version of any included sub-routers (`_IncludedRouter.original_router`) to detect changes anywhere in the router tree—this check is O(number of included routers), much cheaper than regenerating the whole OpenAPI schema.

So as long as no routes have been added/changed since the last call, `openapi()` skips calling `get_openapi()` entirely and just returns the cached dict.
